title: Return Values & void
summary: Send computed results back to the caller using return statements, and understand void for side-effect-only procedures.
learningOutcomes: Return typed results from methods to callers
Use early returns to reduce nested indentation
Handle side-effect methods correctly with void

activities.title: Core Mechanics: Return Values & void

breakdown.whatIsIt: Comprehensive exploration of Return Values & void in Java.
breakdown.whyItMatters: Crucial for writing maintainable, reusable, and bug-free Java applications.
howItWorks: Decomposes complex logic into self-contained subprograms.
Allocates local variables on Call Stack frames.
Passes arguments by value, copying parameter data into frames.
Returns execution control back to caller upon reaching return statement.
keyTakeaways: Mastering Return Values & void is essential for Java placement interviews and clean architecture.
Methods enforce the DRY principle by eliminating redundant duplicate code.
Parameters act as local placeholders; arguments provide runtime values.
Always consider edge cases such as invalid input parameters or stack overflow.

activities.title: Verified Java Implementation: Return Values & void
activities.description: Watch how early return statements terminate execution before reaching downstream logic.

questions.prompt: What is the mandatory compiler rule for a method with return type 'int'?
options: It must print an integer to the console
Every reachable execution path must terminate with a return statement that returns an int
It can only take int parameters
It must return 0
questions.explanation: If a method declares a return type, every single possible execution path through the method must return a compatible value.

questions.prompt: What happens if code is placed immediately after an unconditional return statement inside the same block?
options: It executes when the program closes
The compiler raises an 'unreachable statement' error
It executes only on Sundays
It is automatically commented out by the JVM
questions.explanation: The Java compiler detects unreachable code following an unconditional return statement and raises a compile-time error.

questions.prompt: Can a method with return type 'void' contain a 'return;' statement?
options: No, return is completely illegal in void methods
Yes, 'return;' with no value can be used to exit the method early
Yes, but only if it returns null
Yes, but only inside a switch statement
questions.explanation: In void methods, 'return;' is valid and serves as an early exit mechanism.

questions.prompt: What is a 'Guard Clause' in method design?
options: A security firewall preventing hacker methods
An early return check at the start of a method to handle invalid conditions or edge cases immediately
A try-catch block wrapping every statement
A comment guarding against code deletion
questions.explanation: Guard clauses check preconditions at the top of a method and return early, preventing deep nested if/else pyramids.

questions.prompt: Given: 'public static boolean isPositive(int n) { if (n > 0) return true; }'. Why does this fail to compile?
options: boolean cannot be returned from static methods
Missing return statement if n <= 0
Variable n is not declared
if statement cannot contain return
questions.explanation: If n <= 0, the method reaches the end of its body without returning a boolean. Java requires all paths to return a value.

questions.prompt: Can a method return a calculated expression directly, e.g., 'return (a + b) * 2;'?
options: No, you must always store it in a variable first
Yes, the expression is evaluated and its resulting value is returned directly
Only for String concatenation
Only if parentheses are omitted
questions.explanation: Any valid expression matching the return type can be returned directly without creating an intermediate local variable.

questions.prompt: What value can a method with return type 'double' return?
options: Only double literals
double values or narrower numeric types like int and float that widen automatically
String representations of doubles
Only positive numbers
questions.explanation: A double method can return double values, as well as int, long, or float values which widen to double automatically.

questions.prompt: How do you capture the return value of a method call in the caller?
options: Assign the method call to a variable of matching type: 'int res = calculate(x);'
Use the 'capture' keyword
Call the method without parentheses
Return values are automatically printed and cannot be captured
questions.explanation: The return value replaces the method call expression at runtime and can be assigned to a variable, used in expressions, or passed to other methods.

Return larger of a or b.

interviewQA.question: What is the return contract in Java?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: If a method specifies any return type other than void, the compiler guarantees that every possible execution path through the method body terminates with a return statement yielding a value compatible with the declared type. Failing this check triggers a compile-time error.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: Why is 'unreachable code' an error in Java?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: The Java Language Specification (JLS) forbids unreachable statements. If code appears directly after an unconditional return, break, continue, or throw, the compiler halts with an 'unreachable statement' error to prevent dead logic and programmer confusion.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: How do early returns improve code quality compared to nested if-else structures?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Early returns (Guard Clauses) handle edge cases, error states, and invalid arguments at the very start of a method and return immediately. This eliminates deeply nested conditional blocks, flattens code structure, reduces cyclomatic complexity, and makes the happy path obvious.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: Can a method return multiple values in Java?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: No. A Java method can return at most one value. To return multiple pieces of data, developers wrap them in a custom class, a Java record (Java 14+), an array, or a collection (like List or Map).
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: What happens if a void method executes 'return;' without any value?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Execution of the void method terminates immediately, and control returns to the caller. It is completely legal and commonly used as a guard clause.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: Can you use a method call as an argument to another method?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Yes. If methodA() returns a type that methodB() expects, you can compose them directly: methodB(methodA()). The inner method executes first, and its returned value is passed as the argument to the outer method.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: Can a finally block override a return statement in Java?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Yes. If a return statement is executed inside a try block, and the corresponding finally block also contains a return statement, the return from the finally block overrides the try block's return. This is considered an anti-pattern and should be avoided.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

activities.title: Self-Mastery Checklist
checklist: Return Contract: Every possible path in a non-void method must return a value of matching type.
void Methods: Used for procedures with side effects. They return no value, but can use 'return;' for early exits.
Guard Clauses: Checking edge conditions early and returning immediately flattens nested if/else logic.
Unreachable Code: Statements placed immediately after unconditional return statements cause compile-time errors.
Value Composition: Method return values can be assigned to variables, printed, or passed directly into other methods.
